UK-Spec Ford Ranger Raptor V6 EcoBoost Hits 621 BHP With Stage 3 Kit That Includes Garrett Turbos
12 photos
Photo: Motorsport and Performance
As you're well aware, the Ranger Raptor with the 3.0-liter EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 can't do better than 288 brake horsepower from the factory due to gasoline particulate filters indirectly mandated by strict emission standards. UK-based tuner Motorsport and Performance, however, can fix that. Opting for the Stage 3 kit can unleash up to 621 brake horsepower, which is quite a tremendous jump.
Advertised with anything from 600 to 630 ponies, the Stage 3 package builds on two lesser stages. The first one involves only software, with customers offered a choice between 400, 450, and 475-bhp calibrations. The 450 appears to be the most popular, or so claims Motorsport and Performance big kahuna Ben Dunn.
Stage 2 involves new hardware, including an upgraded intercooler that better controls intake air temperature under sustained boost. A cold air intake and MAP x Keltec catted downpipes also need mentioning, along with estimates of 520 to 540 brake horsepower. Upgrading to Stage 3 status requires new turbochargers.
A pair of Garrett-supplied snails are on the menu, specifically PowerMax GT1752S units. The direct-fit spinny lads are said to flow 18 percent more air compared to factory turbos, and the Stage 3 upgrade further replaces the factory-issue plastic charge pipes with aluminum hot- and cold-side piping. Under increased boost pressure, going for aluminum sounds like a very good idea.
Building on the Stage 2 kit, Stage 3 also comes with bespoke engine and transmission control unit calibrations. The customer who supplied the development Ranger Raptor also specified a Manta turbo-back exhaust system, which definitely sounds better than the stock exhaust. High-flow cats are featured, allowing the six-cylinder lump to exhale better.
Photo: Motorsport and Performance This Manta exhaust retains the bi-modal exhaust valves from the factory, so the driver can switch between quiet and rowdy whenever they feel like it. Motorsport and Performance lists the Stage 3 package at 10,499 pounds sterling, whereas the aftermarket exhaust adds another 2,400 on top.
Customers are required to allow one to two weeks for installation and calibration. Fuel choice also matters here, with the British tuner specifying 99-RON E5 gasoline while warning against E10, 95-RON, and 97-RON fuels. Motorsport and Performance further acknowledges that replacing the factory turbos will affect the manufacturer's warranty.
Priced from £51,650 (excluding value-added tax) in the United Kingdom, the Ranger Raptor is advertised by its maker with a 0-60 time of 7.9 seconds. Previously offered with a twin-turbo diesel inline-four mill, the Ranger Raptor lost its lesser diesel engine in early 2026.
Speaking of which, the 2.0-liter EcoBlue was discontinued from all trims in favor of two alternatives. The 3.0-liter EcoBlue remains on sale in the Old Continent, yet Ford of Europe wants prospective customers to believe that the 2.3-liter EcoBoost plug-in hybrid is the direct replacement for the 2.0-liter EcoBlue.
The 3.0-liter EcoBlue is the better choice for maximum towing and payload capacities, offering better highway range than the plug-in hybrid once its high-voltage battery depletes. The six-pot diesel also makes a lot more sense because it produces maximum torque from 1,750 revolutions per minute, giving it effortless and predictable pulling power.
